description:
ecoinvent names its dissolved molybdenum `Molybdenum VI` on thirteen rows, writes the formula `Mo+6` and the synonyms `Molybdenum (+6)` and `Molybdenum ion` on them, and from 3.10.1 on registers every one as 7439-98-7 -- molybdenum the *metal*. Release 3.9.1 shipped the same thirteen uuids under the same name with the ion's own number, 16065-87-5, and every other metal ion in the release carries its ion's number. A stated number outranks a name, so on the 2026-08-29 build of `54b0f9d` all thirteen were published as `Molybdenum`, the element, while the one 3.8 row that 3.12 no longer carries -- `697e8ecf`, in the stratosphere -- is decided by 3.9.1's number and was published as `Molybdenum(6+)`. Fourteen rows of one vendor name, two substances, decided by which release last shipped the row.

The decision the issue asked for: the name is believed, as it was for EF's `vanadium (v)` (#49) and BAFU's `Cadmium II` (#146), and here the vendor's own earlier release says the same. The ion's number is written on the name in the 3.10.1, 3.11 and 3.12 fixes files; `tools/derive_ecoinvent_canonical_identities.py` now reads each release with its fixes applied, so `ecoinvent-canonical-identities.json` carries the ion's number as 3.12's identity and 3.8's plain `Molybdenum` rows under those uuids follow it at matching. (Until #398. 3.8 wrote the metal's number on those rows, and a uuid whose number moves from the element to the ion is two flows, so they are the metal; the 3.8 claim below is rewritten to say so.) EF 3.1 publishes `molybdenum (vi)` in all thirteen contexts, so every row lands on a flow that exists. See #181.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.12's thirteen Molybdenum VI rows reach hexavalent molybdenum by the corrected number
expectations.comment: Before: `algorithm` on `basis: cas` too -- but on 7439-98-7, landing on `Molybdenum`. `basis: cas` is claimed so that a later change reaching the ion by reading the roman numeral off the name would fail here: the number is corrected, the name is not interpreted. Selected by the corrected number since #398 rather than by name: the name the merge records for these rows is the label enrichment gives them, which read `Molybdenum VI` on the build of `43403ac` and `Molybdenum(6+)` on the build of `bb21bfa`, and the claim is about where the rows land, not about that spelling.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.8's fourteen Molybdenum emissions under these uuids are the metal 3.8 named
expectations.comment: Rewritten on #398, keeping the id: this claim used to say the opposite. 3.8 names these fourteen rows plain `Molybdenum` under 7439-98-7, the metal, and until #398 the canonical-identities file read them as 3.12's corrected `Molybdenum VI`, 16065-87-5, so they reached the ion. The number moving from the element to the ion is now a second substance under a reused uuid, and 3.8's rows keep the element they were published with -- where BAFU's fourteen `Molybdenum` rows already are (the claim below). Fifteen rows: the fourteen emissions and the `Molybdenum, in ground` resource, which the merge records as `Molybdenum`. On the build of `43403ac` the fourteen were recorded as `Molybdenum VI` and reached fo-38bf6545e590d631, Molybdenum(6+).

expectations.title: ecoinvent's Molybdenum resource row still reaches the metal
expectations.comment: The leave-alone half. `Molybdenum` in the ground, 7439-98-7, is the metal and means it; the fix is keyed on the exact name `Molybdenum VI`, so this row cannot move, and this claim is what says so if the key is ever loosened.

expectations.title: BAFU's fourteen Molybdenum rows still reach the metal
expectations.comment: BAFU names no molybdenum ion: its thirteen emission rows and one resource row are all plain `Molybdenum` under 7439-98-7, and a fix in an ecoinvent file cannot reach them. Here because BAFU's emissions and ecoinvent's now differ on purpose -- BAFU says the metal, ecoinvent says the ion -- and that is each vendor's own statement, not a defect.
